data.title: How Much Merck Do You Really Get Through 3 ETFs?
data.description:

Merck just reported that its TroFuse-015 study for sacituzumab tirumotecan in advanced cancer of the stomach and oesophagus met its main goal by helping patients live longer, with safety in line with earlier work. State Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLV)

Those other holdings pull some of your healthcare exposure toward areas like diabetes treatments, consumer health products, medical devices, and research tools rather than one drug portfolio.

One flagged issue for Merck is that its 2.56% dividend is not well covered by earnings. XLV spreads that single company payout risk across dozens of healthcare stocks, so your income stream depends on a wider set of pharmaceutical, biotech, equipment, and managed care dividends. AbbVie, Johnson & Johnson and Eli Lilly shape most of what you own in VHT, alongside a broad mix of pharmaceuticals at 33.7%, biotechnology at 24.1%, and meaningful slices in health care equipment, tools, managed care and services. Merck is the fifth largest position at 4.77%, so roughly US$48 of every US$1,000 goes into Merck, and XLV holds a slightly larger slice. IHE only softens that company specific issue to a degree because almost all of its 99.5% exposure is still in pharmaceuticals, so weak profitability at one large drug business can be partly offset by others whose results depend on different therapies and markets, but sector wide pressure on pricing would still hit much of this ETF at the same time.

Merck through funds means choosing your mix

In all three ETFs, Merck is a modest slice, between about US$42 and US$53 for every US$1,000 you put in, so the real question is what you want around it. XLV gives you that larger Merck stake at the lowest fee, US$8 a year on a US$10,000 holding, with healthcare equipment, tools and managed care alongside pharmaceuticals and biotechnology. Almost everything sits in pharmaceuticals, and its cost is higher at US$37 a year on US$10,000, so your decision is whether a focused drug-heavy portfolio is worth that, given risks such as Merck’s weaker profit margins and clinical news such as the recent positive trial result.
